context v23-v24; result of prior action

items.question: Under what condition does unified consciousness come to shine through pervasive awareness in this sequence?
premises: A force arising from root investigation acts upon the threads of breath when present.
That force produces a self marked by the flash of unity in this manner.
Such a self brings about the shining of pervasive consciousness as a result.
items.inference: When the covering of the breath threads by root-search force is present, a unity-flashing self causes pervasive consciousness to shine.
uncertainties: Exact scope of thread covering remains unclear from this verse alone.
Relation between agent and result is sequential rather than strictly causal.
items.plain_english: When the force of investigating the root covers the threads of breath, the self flashing with unity causes pervasive consciousness to shine.

items.question: What kind of offering must be performed next after the condition described in the preceding verse?
premises: A subsequent step follows the condition established in the prior verse.
That step requires performing a special worship infused with nonduality.
The object of that worship is indeed supreme and steeped in nondual nectar of shiva.
items.inference: Then one must perform a special worship infused with nonduality, for that worship is supreme and steeped in nondual nectar of shiva.
uncertainties: Agent is not named explicitly and must be inferred as the teacher by rite context.
Mode of infusion is not specified by this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Then one must perform a special worship infused with nonduality, for that worship is supreme and steeped in the nondual nectar of shiva.

items.question: By means of which offering materials does the nondual view of shiva act as purification for the animal offering?
premises: The materials used are argha, flower, fragrance and the like, including liquor, by means of that offering.
In relation to the animal offering, a particular view comes into play.
That view of nonduality of shiva is purification and makes the offering supreme.
items.inference: By means of those offering materials, the view of nonduality of shiva serves as purification for the animal offering and renders it supreme.
uncertainties: Exact relation between liquor and the view is not explicit and remains open.
Rite status of the animal is not redefined here beyond the context given.
items.plain_english: By means of argha, flowers, fragrance, liquor and the like, the view of the nonduality of shiva purifies the animal offering and makes it supreme.

items.question: What range of things is to be offered before the lord in accordance with this rite?
premises: The teacher is to offer before the lord living beings and elements arisen from that source.
These are to be offered whether perfected, unperfected, mixed, or otherwise.
Whatever is moving or stationary may fall within that offering as appropriate.
items.inference: Before the lord, one is to offer lives and elements arisen from that source, in perfected, unperfected, mixed or other forms, including whatever is moving or stationary.
uncertainties: Degree of literalness for 'living beings' is not resolved by this verse alone.
Selection criteria among the listed items remain unspecified.
items.plain_english: One should offer before the lord lives and elements arisen from that source, whether perfected, unperfected, mixed, or whatever else there may be, moving or stationary.

items.question: What status does the qualified hero-animal attain after passing through the listed rite actions?
premises: The hero-animal has been seen, sprinkled, witnessed, obtained, taken up and joined by rite actions.
Through those actions it is extinguished in the sense required by this rite.
As a result it attains a status described as eightfold, higher and supreme.
items.inference: The hero-animal, qualified by seeing, sprinkling, witnessing, obtaining, taking up and joining, is extinguished by rite action and attains an eightfold, higher, supreme status.
uncertainties: Technical meaning of extinguished is not defined by this verse alone.
Eightfold status cannot be unpacked from this verse and remains open.
items.plain_english: The hero-animal, having been seen, sprinkled, witnessed, obtained, taken up and joined in the rite, is extinguished and attains a status that is eightfold, higher and supreme.

items.question: To whom may the offering used for shiva be given or consumed, according to this sequential rule?
premises: In order, that which is used for shiva is not to be given to the unworthy under any circumstance.
Indeed, not everyone is worthy to eat an offering used for shiva.
The restriction applies sequentially and without exception.
items.inference: In order and without exception, an offering used for shiva is not to be given to the unworthy, for not everyone is worthy to eat it.
uncertainties: Criteria for unworthy are not specified by this verse alone.
Boundary between giving and eating is treated together but not distinguished here.
items.plain_english: In order and never otherwise, an offering used for shiva is not to be given to the unworthy, for not everyone is worthy to eat it.

items.question: What status does someone attain who, even without initiation, eats the offering impelled by will of shiva and rite?
premises: Even one devoid of initiation may act if impelled by will of shiva and rite.
If such a person eats by devotion, an action is performed under that condition.
That person becomes complete, a samaya-initiate, and well cultivated.
items.inference: Whoever, even without initiation, is impelled by will of shiva and rite and eats by devotion becomes complete, a samaya-initiate, and well cultivated.
uncertainties: Relation between eating by devotion and initiation status is asserted here but not argued.
Distinction between samaya-initiate status and higher statuses remains open in this verse.
items.plain_english: Whoever, even without initiation, is impelled by the will of shiva and by rite and eats by devotion becomes complete, a samaya-initiate, and well cultivated.

items.question: By what means is the offering seen, looked upon and sprinkled in this rite?
premises: The offering is seen and looked upon by means of an offering of the eye kindled by rays.
It is sprinkled, and only so.
That sprinkling is indeed done by drops from an argha vessel.
items.inference: The offering is seen and looked upon by an offering of the eye kindled by rays, and it is sprinkled only by drops from an argha vessel.
uncertainties: Exact function of the eye offering is not explained by this verse alone.
Relation between seeing and sprinkling remains sequential rather than explicit.
items.plain_english: The offering is seen and looked upon by an offering of the eye kindled by rays, and it is sprinkled only with drops from an argha vessel.

items.question: What action is prescribed for the qualified seer who has commenced the rite after purification by the spoken triad?
premises: The complete seer has shown the properly worshipped mandala in full.
That seer has commenced the rite and is purified by the spoken triad.
Such a seer is also to perform the action of shaking.
items.inference: The complete seer, who has shown the fully and properly worshipped mandala, has commenced the rite and is purified by the spoken triad, and is to shake as prescribed.
uncertainties: Object of shaking is not named by this verse alone.
Identity of the spoken triad remains open without wider context.
items.plain_english: The complete seer, who has shown the mandala properly worshipped in full, has commenced the rite and been purified by the spoken triad, and should also shake.

items.question: In what order of effects may the offering behave when taken up in the presence of sacrifice and pacified by weapons and winds?
premises: When taken up in the presence of sacrifice, the offering may behave in order.
It may tremble, or when stiffened it may flow, or it may be dissolved.
In that process it is pacified by weapons and winds.
items.inference: In order, when taken up in the presence of sacrifice, the offering may tremble, or when stiffened may flow, or may be dissolved, and is pacified by weapons and winds.
uncertainties: Weapons and winds are technical here and not explained by this verse alone.
Causal link between the three effects and pacification remains open.
items.plain_english: In order, when the offering is taken up in the presence of sacrifice, it may tremble, or when stiffened it may flow, or it may be dissolved, and it is pacified by weapons and winds.

items.question: By what method is the offering joined to shiva and extinguished in this rite?
premises: The offering is joined by the order of abandoning cause and by joining to shiva.
It is extinguished by that joining.
This is done through an offering of breath and mind made by a guru after practice.
items.inference: The offering is joined by abandoning cause in order and by joining to shiva, and is extinguished through an offering of breath and mind made by a guru after practice.
uncertainties: Exact sequence of abandoning cause is not detailed by this verse alone.
Agency split between guru and others remains to be fixed by wider context.
items.plain_english: The offering is joined by abandoning cause in order and by joining to shiva, and is extinguished through the offering of breath and mind made by a guru after practice.

items.question: By what means and in what mode is the supreme form to be resorted to at the beginning of this action?
premises: At first, by the south fire and by dissolution through the net of gentle kala, an action is prescribed.
That action is to resort to the supreme form.
It is to be done by becoming one with that form.
items.inference: Thus, at first, by the south fire and by dissolution through the net of gentle kala, one should resort to the supreme form by becoming one with it.
uncertainties: Identity of the south fire is technical and not defined by this verse alone.
Net of gentle kala remains open without reference to the fixed lists in this ahnika.
items.plain_english: Thus, at first, by the south fire and by dissolution through the net of gentle kala, one should resort to the supreme form by becoming one with it.
